column1: # domain    defaults domain; a leading / makes it system-wide (written via sudo)
# profiles  comma-separated: dev, ai, desktop ("all" is not special — list them)
#           major-version gating ("-" = open-ended). When Apple renames or
#           kills a key, fill in max_macos with the last release that still
#           honors it — the entry then reports as a version-filtered skip on
#           newer systems instead of a spurious read-back mismatch. The audit
#           you which keys to gate: compare audits across macOS releases.
# host      "-" for the per-user domain, "currentHost" for -currentHost writes
# note      free text, ignored by the engine
# Value tokens: {HOME} and {SCREENSHOTS_DIR} are expanded at write time.
# {SCREENSHOTS_DIR} comes from SETUP_SCREENSHOT_DIR (config file or env),
# defaulting to ~/Desktop — same for SETUP_TIMEZONE, consumed by the time
# action in defaults.sh. Nothing machine-specific is hardcoded here.
# Every write is verified by read-back (see lib/common.sh); result per key
# is appended to the audit file for CI matrices. Keys that need more than a
# single defaults write (FDA-gated domains, PlistBuddy paths, systemsetup)
# are actions in defaults.sh and audit-report themselves as plain text.
